<p id="Sx1.SS2.p8.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of tasks, <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T,i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the hallucination of <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task on the model trained after <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>-th task, <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i,i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the hallucination of <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task on the model trained after <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task; <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{T,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{T,i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the instruction unfollowing of <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task on the model trained after <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>-th task, <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{i,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{i,i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the instruction unfollowing of <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task on the model trained after <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task; <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{T,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{T,i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the other errors of <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task on the model trained after <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>-th task, <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{i,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{i,i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the other errors of <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task on the model trained after <math id="Sx1.SS2.p8.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th task. We prompt the Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct model to determine which type the error belongs to (prompts are shown in Figure <a href="#Sx1.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, Figure <a href="#Sx1.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, and Figure <a href="#Sx1.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>

<p id="Sx1.SS3.p1.9" class="ltx_p">(2) Setting of LoRA based methods are as follows:</p>

<div id="lstnumberx81" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx81.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">        </span><span id="lstnumberx81.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">r</span><span id="lstnumberx81.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">:</span><span id="lstnumberx81.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx81.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">32</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx82" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx82.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">        </span><span id="lstnumberx82.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">lora_alpha</span><span id="lstnumberx82.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">:</span><span id="lstnumberx82.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx82.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">32</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx83" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx83.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">        </span><span id="lstnumberx83.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">lora_dropout</span><span id="lstnumberx83.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">:</span><span id="lstnumberx83.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx83.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">0.05</span>
</div>
</div>
<p id="Sx1.SS3.p1.11" class="ltx_p">It should be noted that all methods maintain an equal scale of trainable parameters. Although MoELoRA and MAGE introduce multi-experts mechanism, the total number of LoRA ranks remains the same as other baseline methods based on single LoRA paradigm. For instance, we set 4 experts in MoELoRA and MAGE, each LoRA rank is set to 8, maintaining the same total number of LoRA ranks as other baselines of 32.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.4 </span>Baseline Details</h3>

<div id="Sx1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Zero-Shot</span> means using the SEED-X model with original pre-trained checkpoints to obtain the zero-shot performance. <span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LoRA Fine-Tune</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite> prepends the LoRA parameter efficient tuning paradigm into MLLM; <span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MoELoRA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite> is based on the multi-expert mechanism, and the number of experts for each MoE layer is set to 4; <span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LAE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite></span> adopts the stable EMA weight to update the LoRA parameters, which is set to 0.99. <span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EWC</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite> considers the change of the training parameters and utilizes the specific parameters changing loss as a regularization penalty. <span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PGP</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite> introduces a gradient projection method for efficient parameters, and changes the gradient direction orthogonal to the previous feature subspace. <span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CIA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite> proposes dynamic EMA weight update strategy and instruction grouping mechanism. Considering that CIA extra incorporates the instruction grouping mechanism, which expands LoRA parameters. To make a fair comparison with other non-model expansion methods, we specifically remove the instruction grouping mechanism. <span id="Sx1.SS4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RegLoRA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite> identifies important LoRA parameters and applies dynamic regularization masks to limit disruptive updates, thereby stabilizing key weights to preserve prior knowledge and mitigate catastrophic forgetting.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.5 </span>Training Orders</h3>

<div id="Sx1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To validate the robustness of our method, we adopt the following three types of training orders.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">1). Origin training order: VQAv2, ImageNet, Flickr30k, RefCOCO, OCRVQA, HQEdit.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">2). Reverse training order: HQEdit, OCRVQA, RefCOCO, Flickr30k, ImageNet, VQAv2.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">3). Alphabet training order: Flickr30k, HQEdit, ImageNet, OCRVQA, RefCOCO, VQAv2.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.6 </span>Mathematical Deduction</h3>

<div id="Sx1.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 1:</span> Let <math id="Sx1.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(\theta;x)=\log p(x;\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(\theta;x)=\log p(x;\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> be the log-likelihood for a single sample and <math id="Sx1.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s(\theta;x)=\nabla_{\theta}\ell(\theta;x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(\theta;x)=\nabla_{\theta}\ell(\theta;x)</annotation></semantics></math> be the gradient. Under standard regularity conditions that allow for the interchange of integration and differentiation, the Fisher information matrix (as shown in Eq.(<a href="#Sx1.E11" title="In 9.6 Mathematical Deduction ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>)):</p>
<table id="Sx1.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{X\sim p(\cdot;\theta)}\!\left[s(\theta;X)s(\theta;X)^{\top}\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{X\sim p(\cdot;\theta)}\!\left[s(\theta;X)s(\theta;X)^{\top}\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">is equal to the negative expected Hessian of the log-likelihood (as shown in Eq.(<a href="#Sx1.E12" title="In 9.6 Mathematical Deduction ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>)):</p>
<table id="Sx1.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\theta)=-\mathbb{E}\big[\nabla^{2}_{\theta}\ell(\theta;X)\big]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\theta)=-\mathbb{E}\big[\nabla^{2}_{\theta}\ell(\theta;X)\big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof 1:</span> Since the likelihood is normalized, we have <math id="Sx1.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int p(x;\theta)\,dx=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int p(x;\theta)\,dx=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiating both sides with respect to <math id="Sx1.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> yields:</p>
<table id="Sx1.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="Sx1.E13"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="Sx1.E13.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle 0=\nabla_{\theta}\int p(x;\theta)\,dx=\int\nabla_{\theta}p(x;\theta)\,dx=\int p(x;\theta)\,s(\theta;x)\,dx," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo>∫</mo></mstyle><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo>∫</mo></mstyle><msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo>∫</mo></mstyle><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle 0=\nabla_{\theta}\int p(x;\theta)\,dx=\int\nabla_{\theta}p(x;\theta)\,dx=\int p(x;\theta)\,s(\theta;x)\,dx,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Eq.(<a href="#Sx1.E13" title="In 9.6 Mathematical Deduction ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>) implies that:</p>
<table id="Sx1.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[s(\theta;X)]=0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[s(\theta;X)]=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Differentiating this identity again with respect to <math id="Sx1.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and interchanging integration
and differentiation gives that:</p>
<table id="Sx1.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0=\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{E}\big[s(\theta;X)\big]=\int\nabla_{\theta}\!\left(p(x;\theta)\,s(\theta;x)\right)\!dx." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>𝔼</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mpadded style="width:0.219em;" width="0.219em"><mo>)</mo></mpadded></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0=\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{E}\big[s(\theta;X)\big]=\int\nabla_{\theta}\!\left(p(x;\theta)\,s(\theta;x)\right)\!dx.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p2.4" class="ltx_p">Expanding the derivative, we have:</p>
<table id="Sx1.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0=\int(\nabla_{\theta}p)\,s\,dx+\int p\,\nabla_{\theta}s\,dx." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0=\int(\nabla_{\theta}p)\,s\,dx+\int p\,\nabla_{\theta}s\,dx.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p2.5" class="ltx_p">Using <math id="Sx1.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\theta}p(x;\theta)=p(x;\theta)s(\theta;x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\theta}p(x;\theta)=p(x;\theta)s(\theta;x)</annotation></semantics></math>, we have:</p>
<table id="Sx1.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="Sx1.E17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="Sx1.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle 0=\int p\,ss^{\top}\,dx+\int p\,\nabla_{\theta}s\,dx=\mathbb{E}[s(\theta;X)s(\theta;X)^{\top}]+\mathbb{E}[\nabla_{\theta}s(\theta;X)]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mstyle><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mstyle></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle 0=\int p\,ss^{\top}\,dx+\int p\,\nabla_{\theta}s\,dx=\mathbb{E}[s(\theta;X)s(\theta;X)^{\top}]+\mathbb{E}[\nabla_{\theta}s(\theta;X)].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p2.6" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="Sx1.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\theta}s(\theta;x)=\nabla_{\theta}^{2}\ell(\theta;x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\theta}s(\theta;x)=\nabla_{\theta}^{2}\ell(\theta;x)</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain:</p>
<table id="Sx1.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\theta)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[s(\theta;X)s(\theta;X)^{\top}\right]=-\mathbb{E}\!\left[\nabla^{2}_{\theta}\ell(\theta;X)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\theta)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[s(\theta;X)s(\theta;X)^{\top}\right]=-\mathbb{E}\!\left[\nabla^{2}_{\theta}\ell(\theta;X)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Thus, <span id="Sx1.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof 1</span> holds.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The Hessian matrix <math id="Sx1.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(\theta)=\nabla^{2}_{\theta}L(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(\theta)=\nabla^{2}_{\theta}L(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> (or its negative) may be singular or ill-conditioned in practice, which prevents direct use of <math id="Sx1.SS6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(\theta)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(\theta)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. A common remedy is to use a <em id="Sx1.SS6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">regularized inverse</em> of the form:</p>
<table id="Sx1.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big(H(\theta)+\lambda I\big)^{-1},\qquad\lambda&gt;0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big(H(\theta)+\lambda I\big)^{-1},\qquad\lambda&gt;0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p4.2" class="ltx_p">referred to as Tikhonov/ridge regularization or damping. The following statements make the mathematical properties of this regularization explicit.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.SS6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 1:</span> Let <math id="Sx1.SS6.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> be a real symmetric matrix with eigen-decomposition <math id="Sx1.SS6.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H=Q\operatorname{diag}(\mu_{1},\dots,\mu_{d})Q^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H=Q\operatorname{diag}(\mu_{1},\dots,\mu_{d})Q^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="Sx1.SS6.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> is orthogonal and <math id="Sx1.SS6.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mu_{1},\dots,\mu_{d}\in\mathbb{R}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mu_{1},\dots,\mu_{d}\in\mathbb{R}\}</annotation></semantics></math> are the eigenvalues. For any <math id="Sx1.SS6.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, the eigenvalues of <math id="Sx1.SS6.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H+\lambda I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H+\lambda I</annotation></semantics></math> are <math id="Sx1.SS6.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{i}+\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{i}+\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>. In particular, we have the following properties:</p>
<ol id="Sx1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="Sx1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> is chosen so that <math id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{i}+\lambda\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{i}+\lambda\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H+\lambda I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H+\lambda I</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible and we have:</p>
<table id="Sx1.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="Sx1.E20"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="Sx1.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle(H+\lambda I)^{-1}=Q\,\operatorname{diag}\big((\mu_{1}+\lambda)^{-1},\dots,(\mu_{d}+\lambda)^{-1}\big)Q^{\top}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle(H+\lambda I)^{-1}=Q\,\operatorname{diag}\big((\mu_{1}+\lambda)^{-1},\dots,(\mu_{d}+\lambda)^{-1}\big)Q^{\top}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
<li id="Sx1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;-\min_{i}\{\mu_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;-\min_{i}\{\mu_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H+\lambda I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H+\lambda I</annotation></semantics></math> is positive definite; in particular choosing <math id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> guarantees invertibility whenever <math id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\min_{i}\{\mu_{i}\}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{i}\{\mu_{i}\}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.SS6.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof 2</span>: Considering that <math id="Sx1.SS6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is symmetric and has the orthogonal eigen decomposition <math id="Sx1.SS6.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H=Q\operatorname{diag}(\mu_{i})Q^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H=Q\operatorname{diag}(\mu_{i})Q^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have:</p>
<table id="Sx1.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="Sx1.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H+\lambda I=Q\operatorname{diag}(\mu_{i}+\lambda)Q^{\top}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H+\lambda I=Q\operatorname{diag}(\mu_{i}+\lambda)Q^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Sx1.SS6.p6.2" class="ltx_p">so the eigenvalues are <math id="Sx1.SS6.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mu_{i}+\lambda)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mu_{i}+\lambda)</annotation></semantics></math>. The matrix is invertible if none of these eigenvalues vanish, which yields item 1. Item 2 follows because if <math id="Sx1.SS6.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;-\min_{i}\{\mu_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;-\min_{i}\{\mu_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="Sx1.SS6.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{i}+\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{i}+\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="Sx1.SS6.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence <math id="Sx1.SS6.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H+\lambda I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H+\lambda I</annotation></semantics></math> is positive definite.</p>
</div>
<figure id="Sx1.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18055v1/orders.svg" id="Sx1.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/138;" width="429" height="138"></object>

</figure>
<figure id="Sx1.F9" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

</figure>
</section>
<section id="Sx1.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.7 </span>Distinctions and Advantages of Continual-NExT</h3>

<div id="Sx1.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Compared to the previous Continual Instruction Tuning (CIT) frameworks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Continual-NExT has the following key distinctions and advantages: (1). Applicability to a wider range of MLLMs. CIT frameworks are limited to evaluating MLLMs that only produce text modality output (<span id="Sx1.SS7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.</span>, LLaVA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>, QWen-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>), while Continual-NExT extends support to vision-language generative MLLMs (<span id="Sx1.SS7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.</span>, SEED-X), significantly expanding its applicability. (2). Applicability to a wider range of tasks. CIT focuses solely on incremental tasks related to text generation (<span id="Sx1.SS7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.</span>, VQA), resulting in high inter-task similarity and limited diversity. In contrast, Continual-NExT additionally introduces image generation tasks (<span id="Sx1.SS7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.</span>, Image Editing). This inclusion greatly enhances task diversity and first breaks the modality boundary in continual learning by integrating multimodal generative tasks within a unified framework.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.8 </span>Additional Experiments</h3>

<div id="Sx1.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To better present the results, we supplement the results of all baselines and ours training after each task (stage) and testing on previous tasks (stages) in Table <a href="#Sx1.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, Table <a href="#Sx1.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, Table <a href="#Sx1.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, Table <a href="#Sx1.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, Table <a href="#Sx1.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, Table <a href="#Sx1.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>, Table <a href="#Sx1.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, and Table <a href="#Sx1.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>. Additionally, we visualize the Avg.ACC and Forgetting performance of different methods across stages in Figure <a href="#Sx1.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.6 Mathematical Deduction ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">From both the Tables and the Figure, we observe that MAGE consistently outperforms the LoRA baseline at all stages, demonstrating superior continual learning capability and stronger resistance to catastrophic forgetting. Compared with other baselines, MAGE exhibits slightly inferior Avg.ACC performance in the first one or two stages, but gradually surpasses all baselines and achieves a clear performance lead in later stages.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We attribute this phenomenon to the freezing of a subset of model parameters. As a result, MAGE’s ability to adapt to newly introduced tasks is constrained. In the early stages of Unified Comprehension and Generation Continual Learning, where the number of tasks is limited, Avg.ACC is more sensitive to New.ACC. As a result, MAGE’s lower New.ACC leads to slightly weaker Avg.ACC in the initial stages. However, as the number of tasks increases, Forgetting becomes the dominant factor influencing Avg.ACC. Benefiting from its stronger anti-forgetting capability, MAGE progressively reduces performance degradation on previous tasks, allowing its Avg.ACC to steadily improve and ultimately outperform all other baselines.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS8.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS8.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We also compare the continual learning performance between MAGE with the PEMA update and MAGE with the DEMA update under three distinct training orders in Figure <a href="#Sx1.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 9.6 Mathematical Deduction ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>. Experimental results present that our PEMA can achieve higher Accuracy in each task compared to the DEMA update with fewer storage space and computation cost.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS8.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS8.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We visualize the LoRA baseline’s performance on a set of comprehension and generation tests after the training of each task in Figure <a href="#Sx1.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>. Training on certain tasks causes the model to rapidly forget previously acquired knowledge, leading to failure on some tasks. In contrast, training on other tasks facilitates positive knowledge transfer, enabling the model to recall previously learned capabilities, and thus achieving strong performance on related tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS8.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS8.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The overall algorithmic pipeline of the proposed MAGE method is summarized in <span id="Sx1.SS8.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.SS8.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SS8.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We report the descriptive statistics about our results (<span id="Sx1.SS8.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.</span>, mean and standard deviation of each metric across different methods) in Table <a href="#Sx1.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 9.8 Additional Experiments ‣ Appendix ‣ Continual-NExT: A Unified Comprehension And Generation Continual Learning Framework" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>. Results are obtained from three runs with distinct random seeds.</p>
</div>
<figure id="Sx1.F10" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx1.F10.pic1" class="ltx_picture ltx_centering" height="588.47" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 588.47" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,588.47) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 1.11 L 0 587.37 C 0 587.98 0.5 588.47 1.11 588.47 L 476.27 588.47 C 476.88 588.47 477.38 587.98 477.38 587.37 L 477.38 1.11 C 477.38 0.5 476.88 0 476.27 0 L 1.11 0 C 0.5 0 0 0.5 0 1.11 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 1.11 L 1.11 587.37 L 476.27 587.37 L 476.27 1.11 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 13.35 16.81)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.57em;--ltx-fo-height:40.35em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="561.79" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 558.33)" width="450.68"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.57em;">
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Prompt (Text Generation Task):<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
You are an AI response consistency evaluation agent responsible for categorizing model errors under strict definitions. You are given a question, an answer generated by a model, and its associated label. Your task is to evaluate whether the answer correctly reflects the label and follows the intended instruction in the question.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Error categories are defined as follows:</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Instruction Unfollowing:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> This error occurs when the generated answer fails to follow the semantic intent or constraints of the intended instruction in the question. Such failures are attributed to semantic discrepancies between the instruction and the generated answer.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Hallucination:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> This error occurs when the generated answers wrongly introduce factually incorrect, unsupported, or illusory information that is not grounded in the given label. Hallucinated outputs typically satisfy the syntactic or structural requirements of the instruction, but significantly deviate from the ground-truth facts stated or implied by the content.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Others:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Any error that does not fall into the above two categories should be classified as others.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The question:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {question}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The answer:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {answer}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The label:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {label}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Based on the above definitions, determine:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Whether the generated answers follow the instruction in the question.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Whether hallucination is present.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. If both are present, classify as instruction unfollowing.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Return your decision strictly in JSON format:<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.13.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F10.pic1.1.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{"error_types": ["instruction_not_followed", "hallucination", "others"], "explanation": "…"}</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>

</figure>
<figure id="Sx1.F11" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx1.F11.pic1" class="ltx_picture ltx_centering" height="538.66" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 538.66" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,538.66) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 1.11 L 0 537.55 C 0 538.17 0.5 538.66 1.11 538.66 L 476.27 538.66 C 476.88 538.66 477.38 538.17 477.38 537.55 L 477.38 1.11 C 477.38 0.5 476.88 0 476.27 0 L 1.11 0 C 0.5 0 0 0.5 0 1.11 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 1.11 L 1.11 537.55 L 476.27 537.55 L 476.27 1.11 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 13.35 16.81)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.57em;--ltx-fo-height:36.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="511.98" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 508.52)" width="450.68"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.57em;">
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Prompt (Image Generation Task):<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> You are an AI image generation consistency evaluation agent responsible for categorizing model errors under strict definitions. <span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Error categories are defined as follows:</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Instruction Unfollowing:<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> This error occurs when the generated image fails to follow the semantic intent or constraints of the intended instruction. Such failures are attributed to semantic discrepancies between the instruction and the generated image.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Hallucination:<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> This error occurs when the generated image introduces factually incorrect, unsupported, or illusory information that is not grounded in the given instruction. Hallucinated outputs typically satisfy the syntactic or structural requirements of the instruction, but significantly deviate from the ground-truth facts stated or implied by the content.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Others:<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Any error that does not fall into the above two categories should be classified as others.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The instruction:<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {instruction}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The image:<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {image}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Based on the above definitions, determine:<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Whether the generated image follows the instruction.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Whether hallucination is present.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. If both are present, classify as instruction unfollowing.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Return your decision strictly in JSON format:<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.12.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F11.pic1.1.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{"error_types": ["instruction_not_followed", "hallucination", "others"], "explanation": "…"}</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="Sx1.F11.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="Sx1.F11.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Prompt used for image generation consistency evaluation.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="Sx1.F12" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx1.F12.pic1" class="ltx_picture ltx_centering" height="621.68" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 621.68" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,621.68) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 1.11 L 0 620.58 C 0 621.19 0.5 621.68 1.11 621.68 L 476.27 621.68 C 476.88 621.68 477.38 621.19 477.38 620.58 L 477.38 1.11 C 477.38 0.5 476.88 0 476.27 0 L 1.11 0 C 0.5 0 0 0.5 0 1.11 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.11 1.11 L 1.11 620.58 L 476.27 620.58 L 476.27 1.11 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 13.35 16.81)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.57em;--ltx-fo-height:42.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="595" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 591.54)" width="450.68"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.57em;">
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Prompt (Image Editing Task):<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
You are an AI image editing consistency evaluation agent responsible for identifying errors in edited images under strict definitions. You are given: A source image (the original image before editing). An instruction that describes how the source image should be edited. An edited image generated based on the instruction. Your task is to evaluate whether the edited image correctly reflects the editing instruction when compared to the source image.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Error categories are defined as follows:</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Instruction Unfollowing:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> This error occurs when the edited image fails to follow the semantic intent, constraints, or required modifications described in the instruction. This includes missing required edits, incorrect changes, or changes that contradict the instruction.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Hallucination:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> This error occurs when the edited image introduces new visual elements, attributes, or changes that are not requested or implied by the instruction. The image may appear realistic, but the added content is unsupported by the instruction.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Others:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Any error that does not fall into the above two categories, including minor artifacts or ambiguities that cannot be clearly attributed to instruction unfollowing or hallucination.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The Source Image:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {source_image}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The Instruction:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {instruction}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The Edited Image:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {edited_image}</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Based on the above definitions, determine:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Whether the generated image follows the instruction.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Whether hallucination is present.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. If both are present, classify as instruction unfollowing.</span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Return your decision strictly in JSON format:<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.13.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.F12.pic1.1.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{"error_types": "instruction_not_followed", "hallucination", "others", "explanation": "…"}</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>

<div id="algorithm1.4.3" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="algorithm1.4.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initialize:</span> <math id="algorithm1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{GI}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{GI}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="algorithm1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{GT}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{GT}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="algorithm1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{EI}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{EI}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="algorithm1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{ET}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{ET}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="algorithm1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{con}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{con}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<div id="algorithm1.4.4" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="algorithm1.4.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <em id="algorithm1.4.4.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic"><math id="algorithm1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> = 1, …, <math id="algorithm1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math></em> <span id="algorithm1.4.4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>
